public_rationale: OpenAI's January 31, 2024 report found positive mean accuracy differences with GPT-4 access but reported no statistically significant differences [e1]. Its comparisons of participants reaching the 8/10 threshold also failed to show statistical significance, and it left practical importance uncertain [e1]. Accepting those statistical results, the report supports the narrow claim that it did not rule out a practically important positive effect [e1].
limitations: The report does not establish that a practically important positive effect exists [e1].
The tasks measured information access rather than demonstrating real-world bioweapon creation [e1].
Experts used a research-only GPT-4 variant; the report cautions that the observed gains may not apply to public models [e1].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI has in no way proven that there is no important positive relationship between LLM access and capacity to design bioweapons.

statement.excerpt: Certainly OpenAI has in no way proven that there is not an important positive relationship between LLM access and capacity to design bioweapons, even if you bought the Bonferonni argument, which you shouldn’t.

criteria.support_condition: The study leaves practically important positive effects unresolved, rather than establishing their absence through sufficiently precise estimates and a justified practical threshold.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The study establishes that any positive effect is below a justified threshold of practical importance within the claimed scope.
